resources.string: Exercise runtime primitives directly to verify remember, derived state, produced state, and keyed identity behavior.
This block stays on the default core page so benchmark controls remain visible in the initial viewport.
Stable path: launcher → State scenario → benchmark anchor
Shows local state, a derived label, and text produced from source state.
Verifies ViewModel collaboration through host-provided locals without a manual provider.
The temporary panel keeps its own state while visible and is rebuilt after removal.
Visibility example: hidden when the panel is closed
Drives the first node-level patch targets together so manual tests and benchmarks exercise the same update path.
Patched nodes: Text, Button, TextField, SegmentedControl, TabRow, Row, Column, Box, Image
The Patch scenario keeps the Tab host stable while page metadata changes with state.
Use this page to inspect selected-tab patch behavior across repeated updates.
The stable-key Tab pager preserves page identity; an explicit revision refreshes ordinary captured values.
Advancing Patch state changes the explicit revision, so this page should refresh in isolation.
Use this page to verify that a stable key with a changed revision never retains a stale closure.
VerticalPager also refreshes page content through a stable key and explicit revision.
Verifies that VerticalPager refreshes visible content without a structural change.
After switching to page two, advancing Patch must keep its copy synchronized with external state.
The State chapter should expose whether root rendering, local identity, and conditional reconstruction remain predictable under repeated interaction.
Increment and reset repeatedly; confirm the derived label and timeline update together.
Hide and show the temporary panel; confirm its internal click count is rebuilt.
Open Patch, advance repeatedly, and confirm Text, Button, TextField, SegmentedControl, and TabRow update together.
Switch theme mode and continue interacting; confirm state values survive the theme refresh.
remember state survives under the same identity and is rebuilt after a key change.
derivedStateOf and produceState never lag behind their source state.
The first Patch nodes prefer targeted patching instead of full rebinding.
Conditional UI visibility leaves no stale state behind.
Generic subtree recomposition is not yet more granular.
Patch, rebind, and skipped metrics are not yet visualized directly on the page.
